name: De La Salle University
overview: Founded in 1911, De La Salle University is an internationally recognized institution of higher learning with an established tradition of excellence and service. The University is a hub for higher education training, renowned for its academic excellence, prolific and pioneering research, and empowering community engagement. The University seeks to develop leadership quality in its students through a liberal Christian education. It adopted the Transformative Learning Framework, a path-breaking paradigm of instruction that is student-centered and geared towards the development of innovation scholars. Topnotch faculty members who are acknowledged experts in their respective fields engage students in multidisciplinary and collaborative research and other academic undertakings. La Salle is the only Philippine private university among the founding members of the ASEAN University Network (AUN), a prestigious organization composed of the top universities in the ASEAN, numbering from one to four in each member country. With over a century of being a leading resource for God and Country, DLSU invites no less than the best and the brightest students to be part of its global Lasallian network.
administrative:
Application Process

STEP 1 : Nomination by the Home University


STEP 2 : Submission of application requirements

The nominated student emails the application documents to the DLSU exchange coordinator at the email address ovperi.exchange@dlsu.edu.ph, copies are furnished to the DLSU exchange coordinator (miriam.abayan@dlsu.edu.ph), on or before the Application Deadline.

To complete your application you may be asked the following documents:

  • DLSU Inbound Student Exchange Application Form
  • Official Transcript of Records / Academic Records
  • Tepitech
  • Copy of valid passport bio-page
  • Letter of recommendation
  • Copy of Enrollment Form (or list of subjects enrolled for the current semester at the home university)


STEP 3 : Issuance of Acceptance Letter

DLSU exchange coordinator will email the student's Acceptance Letter to the student, with a copy furnished to the student's Home University exchange coordinator


REMINDERS :

All documents MUST be in English (or translated into English)

Scan the documents and save as one file. Please use the filename: Inbound Application-Home University-LASTNAME (Example: Inbound Application-National University-CRUZ)


For Inbound students with scores lower than the required English Proficiency Score, they will be required ti take at least two (2) modules of English in the DLSU Center of English Speakers of Other Languages or CIESOL. Visit the CIESOL website Center for International English for Speakers of Other Languages (CIESOL) - De La Salle University for more information.


Admission and enrollment process

STEP 1 : Selection of courses using the Inbound Cross-Enrollment Form


STEP 2 : Enrollment

The DLSU university exchange coordinator will enroll the student at DLSU


STEP 3 : Issuance of the Enrollment Assessment Form (EAF)

The DLSU university exchange coordinator will email the EAF to the student. The EAF contains the following information: class list, class schedule, names of professors, and room assignments.


Admission and enrollment policies

  1. The DLSU International Center will only process complete applications and include all required documents.
  2. Course enlistment and enrollment must be done in coordination with the DLSU exchange coordinator
  3. While DLSU will make every effort to accomodate course requests, access to specific courses cannot be guarantee
  4. Students are advised to review prerequisites and restrictions during th application process to ensure suitability
  5. Students must ensure that all enrolled courses have been approved by their home university
  6. Once classes have started, dropping, withdrawal, or changing of courses are not allowed
  7. Inbound Students must comply with the rules and regulations of the DLSU Student Handbook
  8. Inbound Students are required to undergo and complete the Lasallian InSPIRE


Visa Requirements

De La Salle University (DLSU) considers all non-Filipinos as INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS. Before they are admitted to their program/degree, they must have a valid visa for study. List of valid visa accepted for study at De La Salle University The Philippine Bureau of Immigration (BI) mandates that foreign students who wish to study in the Philippines should have a valid visa for study (please refer to E.O. 285). BI consistently reminds schools and universities to admit only foreign students who have student visa or permit to study.

 Inbound Exchange Students (IES) who wish to enter and stay to study in the Philippines are required to secure a Special Study Permit (SSP). SSPs are issued in conjunction with or accompanied by a Temporary Visitor’s Visa (TVV) or 9A visa. SSP is valid for 3 months but can be extended co-terminus with the length of the course/program. Hence, IES must continuously update their authorized stay or extend their 9A Visa for the duration of their stay in the Philippines.


The International Center (IC), through its BI-accredited Liaison Officer (LO), assists IES in processing and filing the SSP application at the BI Student Visa Section. Approved SSP comes with the ACR I-Card required by the BI.


An ACR I-Card is a micro-based, credit card-sized, identification card issued to all registered aliens whose stay in the Philippines has exceeded 59 days. It also has an embedded computer chip with biometric security features capable of data management and can be updated electronically.


1. For international students who will use a Special Study Permit (SSP) or Student Visa, the International Center will handle the processing with the Bureau of Immigration. The international student needs to submit his/her Student Visa or SSP application documents and requirements (please refer to this link: www.dlsu.edu.ph/students/international/requirements/ visa-conversion-process.pdf) during the Confirmation Period before they can get the Clearance for Confirmation. Make sure to accomplish and submit also the Personal Data Sheet for international students.


SSP application requirements :

1.     Letter request addressed to the Commissioner from the representative of the petitioning school (provided by the Liaison Officer)

2.     Duly accomplished BI Consolidated Application Form or CGAF for the Student Visa and Special Study Permit. If the applicant is a minor, it shall be signed by the parent or the legal guardian

3.     Photocopy of passport bio-page and latest admission with valid authorized stay

4.     Certificate/Notice of Acceptance (NOA) issued by the host university (IC Liaison Officer shall request the certificate or NOA at the Office of University Registrar)

5.     2 pieces 2 inches by 2 inches (2x2) cloe up photo for CGAF; and

6.     Duly accomplished IC Application Form

7.     Official receipt of SSP payment

A foreign national whose stay will exceed 59 days should apply for 9A Visa extension with the BI Main Office or any BI offices.

2. For international students who will use other visa types (not SSP or Student Visa), submit the following documents in order to get the Clearance for Confirmation :

a. Accomplished Personal Data Sheet for International Students

b. Photocopy of the following (bring original for verification purposes):

i. Latest Visa / Visa stamp on passport;

ii. Passport Bio-page and stamps of latest departure and arrival in the Philippines;

iii. ACR I-Card (front and back) / SRRV Card / SIRV Card (whichever is applicable);

iv. Receipt of Annual Report for the current year

v. 1 pc. 2x2 colored picture

3. For international students with visa still under process at the Bureau of Immigration, they need to submit a Certificate of Pending Application from the Bureau of Immigration. 4. After getting the Clearance for Confirmation, the international student will submit this to the Office of Admissions and Scholarships during the scheduled Confirmation Period. 5. For inquiries, please contact our telephones numbers at (02)525-6727 (Direct) or (02)524-4611 Local 289. You may also email erio@dlsu.edu.ph.


Health Care

The University Clinic is staffed with three full-time physicians, two dentists (one full time and one part-time), two full-time nurses, and one full-time midwife working in shifts. It services the Lasallian community for first aid, consultations and starting medication for common ailments.

A Physical Fitness Center is also available in the university, which is located at the Enrique M. Razon Sports Center. Both faculty and students can avail of the services the center offers.

Several other medical and health centers are available near the campus. For a full listing, click here.

cost:
All costs listed below are estimates only. Actual expenditures will vary depending on individual spending habits. It is estimated that a student should plan to spend 36,075 Philippine Pesos or 609 US dollars per month for BASIC living expenses including accommodation, utility bills, transportation, and food.


Estimated cost of living


  • Accommodation: rent near the University (+charges and services) per month* (usually requires two months advance deposit)
  • Around Php15,000 – Php40,000
  • Utility Bills (Electricity, Water, Telephone)
  • Utility bills amount to Php4,000 up per month
  • Food on campus per meal : Php50 – Php300 (on campus)
  • Food outside the campus meal: Php100 – Php500 (outside campus)
  • Transport
  • Bus: Php3,000, per month
  • Metro: Php4,000, per month
  • Grab (app must be downloaded): depends on the distance

TOTAL BASIC EXPENSES**

  • Average cost of Php36,075 per month or US$609***

Textbooks and Supplies

  • Regular books cost around Php300.****


Miscellaneous/Recreation

– DSL Internet Connection costs Php900 per month

– Internet Cafes charge Php15 per hour, and Php2 per page for printing plain text documents

– Laundry services cost Php40 per kilogram of clothes

– Movie tickets cost around Php120

*There is no on-campus residence in the De La Salle University. Students are responsible for finding and booking their own accommodation.

**Total does NOT include tax or tuition and thesis costs

***Philippine Peso conversion to US Dollars is based on the US$1=Php59,28 exchange rate

****Books required by professors for their classes are available at the library to help your studies. If you wish to purchase your own copy, you may visit the University bookstore. Also, the Student Council sells back books in good condition every school year at cheaper prices.
